headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from AutoGPT filesystem/CLI autonomy feeding Plane’s file-backed issue workflows; no direct evidence of a shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell and access the filesystem, while Plane accepts file uploads and handles files/notes. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if AutoGPT writes attacker-controlled text that Plane later renders or processes. Plane’s multiple-instance support does not mitigate instruction hijacking; the pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF AutoGPT writes untrusted content into a file that Plane later imports or displays
IF Plane treats uploaded file contents as trusted instructions or markup
mitigations: Restrict AutoGPT to a dedicated staging directory
Disable file uploads into Plane for untrusted artifacts
Add a manual review step before Plane ingests AutoGPT output
Use content sanitization on any imported text
requires-engineering: add provenance labels from AutoGPT to Plane imports

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress; Plane handles files, images, notes, issues, and tasks. If both touch the same workspace, sensitive artifacts can flow from AutoGPT into Plane’s broader collaboration surface and then out through Plane’s APIs or uploads. No profile field proves isolation, so the shared-workspace leakage pathway is plausible and not blocked by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or mounted volume
IF AutoGPT reads sensitive local files and writes them into Plane-visible artifacts
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces
Remove sensitive files from the shared directory
Turn off Plane file uploads for the session
Limit AutoGPT egress to a test endpoint
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Plane does not write the filesystem but does support multiple instances and broad egress. The main conflict is indirect: AutoGPT may mutate shared files or artifacts that Plane consumes, causing racey overwrites or inconsistent state. Because no locking or shared-resource coordination is documented, uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF AutoGPT and Plane share a writable directory or artifact store
IF Plane instances concurrently read files that AutoGPT rewrites
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate directory
Serialize file handoff with a manual checkpoint
Avoid concurrent edits to shared artifacts
Snapshot files before Plane ingests them
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional handoff

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate outputs from shell/file activity, and Plane can turn files, notes, issues, and tasks into work items. If Plane treats AutoGPT output as authoritative, a mistaken or hallucinated artifact can cascade into incorrect issues or scheduling actions. The pair has no documented verification gate, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF Plane ingests AutoGPT-produced text without human verification
IF AutoGPT output is used to create or update issues/tasks
mitigations: Require human approval before creating Plane items
Cross-check AutoGPT claims against source files
Use a template that separates facts from suggestions
Flag uncertain fields for review
requires-engineering: add validation rules before Plane writes

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. Plane exposes support channels and file uploads, while AutoGPT has filesystem and allowlisted egress, but the profiles do not show a specific regulated-data flow. Because the compliance pathway is not evidenced, this remains low rather than none.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Plane file uploads
IF AutoGPT is configured to move that regulated data across jurisdictions or vendors
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared artifacts
Review retention settings in Plane
Restrict AutoGPT to non-sensitive datasets
Document the data flow before deployment
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
